item.title: Rupee outperforms most Asian peers as foreign inflows boost sentiment
item.description: Rupee strengthens to a seven-month high, supported by foreign portfolio inflows and positive market sentiment despite a stronger US dollar ...
item.dc:creator: Anjali Kumari
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee was among the best-performing Asian currencies on Wednesday, gaining 0.26 per cent against the US dollar, as foreign portfolio inflows into domestic equities and positive sentiment in the non-deliverable forward (NDF) market helped the currency withstand a broadly stronger dollar, said dealers. The rupee settled at 93.69 per dollar, its strongest level since April, against the previous close of 93.94 per dollar. Among major Asian currencies, the rupee was the second-best performer of the day after the South Korean won, which gained 0.72 per cent. The Chinese yuan and Taiwanese dollar appreciated 0.10 per cent and 0.02 per cent, respectively. In comparison, the Indonesian rupiah fell 0.48 per cent, while the Philippine peso declined 0.49 per cent. The rupee has gained 1.19 per cent so far in 2026-27 (FY27), reversing some of the depreciation seen earlier. It has appreciated 1.35 per cent in November so far and 2.28 per cent in the current quarter. However, it remains down 4.07 per cent against the dollar on a calendar-year basis and 5.47 per cent over the past year. The currency has recovered from its record low of 96.96 per dollar touched in May, supported by measures announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and improving foreign portfolio flows. It had come close to breaching that level again last month. The gains came despite a broadly stronger dollar, which was supported by higher-than-expected US inflation data and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials. Expectations of tighter monetary policy in the US have increased, with traders pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike in December and a small possibility of a larger 50-basis-point increase. “A stronger dollar and the prospect of higher US interest rates would typically weigh on emerging market currencies, including the rupee. But the pickup in foreign portfolio investment flows into Indian equities had provided support to the domestic currency,” said a dealer at a state-owned bank. Traders said dollar-selling interest was visible across the market during Wednesday's session, while activity in the NDF market also indicated an improvement in sentiment towards the rupee. Foreign investors have bought nearly $6 billion worth of Indian equities in November so far, marking their highest monthly purchases since September 2024. The inflows have helped improve demand for the rupee and supported its recent recovery. Government bond yields, however, hardened on Wednesday, tracking a sharp rise in US Treasury yields after hotter-than-expected inflation data and short bets ahead of the weekly government bond auction on Friday, said dealers. The yield on the benchmark 10-year government bond rose 6 basis points to 7.21 per cent, while the five-year yield increased 4 basis points to 6.89 per cent. “Traders have built short bets in the 10-year bond ahead of the weekly auction, adding to the pressure on bond prices,” a dealer at a primary dealership said. Traders now eye India's retail inflation data for October, scheduled to be released on Thursday. A higher-than-expected inflation reading could influence expectations around the RBI's monetary policy trajectory, while market participants will also track movements in the dollar and foreign portfolio flows for further cues.

item.title: Moody's retains India's FY27 growth forecast at 7% on resilient demand
item.description: Rating agency cites robust consumption, improving private investment and resilience to the energy shock, but flags inflation, monsoon risks and tighter monetary policy ...
item.dc:creator: Auhona Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Moody’s Ratings on Wednesday retained its growth forecast for the Indian economy at 7 per cent for the financial year 2026-27, citing its resilience to the energy supply shock, robust consumption and signs of a revival in private investment, even as it flagged inflationary pressures and monsoon-related risks to the outlook. In September, it had revised its growth forecast for India to 7 per cent from 6 per cent. In its latest Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, the rating agency said India's broad-based economic momentum and strong macroeconomic fundamentals put it in a position to sustain growth near 7 per cent over the medium term. “Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7 per cent over the medium term. A sustained private investment boom that materially boosts manufacturing, employment and productivity could lift growth rates above our baseline,” it said. The agency’s calendar-year projections also showed the economy growing at 7 per cent in 2026, 2027 and 2028, following an estimated 7.3 per cent expansion in 2025. Moody's attributed India's stronger outlook partly to its ability to adjust to the energy price shock caused by the West Asia conflict. “India has adjusted to the energy price shock better than previously assumed, helped by its ability to diversify crude and gas supplies and buffer consumers from the immediate price impact through state-backed oil marketing companies and tax cuts,” the agency said. India's extensive refining capacity, including the world's largest single-site refinery complex, has helped minimise fuel supply disruptions and enabled the country to remain a major exporter of refined petroleum products, Moody’s added. The agency also flagged signs that India could be on the cusp of a new private capital expenditure cycle after several years of corporate and banking-sector balance-sheet repair. It said robust capital goods production and imports, accelerating industrial credit growth, and rising capacity utilisation pointed to improving investment momentum. “Broader economic activity also remains solid, amid expanding manufacturing and services purchasing manager indexes and double-digit year-on-year growth in goods and services tax revenue, vehicle sales and merchandise exports,” the agency noted. However, the agency flagged near-term risks from rising prices and weakening rural demand. Household consumption remained vulnerable to intensifying and broadening price pressures, with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI's) 2-6 per cent target range, it said. A deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Niño conditions were also likely to weigh on agricultural output and rural demand, the agency noted. “With the RBI on track to raise rates further, tighter monetary policy could delay the recovery in private investment,” Moody’s added. Its projections showed India's annual average inflation easing from 4.5 per cent in 2026 to 4.3 per cent in 2027 and 4 per cent in 2028. India’s GDP grew 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter of FY27, according to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in August. The Finance Ministry, in its October 2026 Monthly Economic Review, raised its FY27 real GDP growth estimate to 7.3 per cent from the 6.8-7.2 per cent range projected in the Economic Survey, citing robust domestic demand and sustained investment activity, while flagging risks from elevated crude oil prices, rising food inflation and uncertainty over the kharif crop. Across G20 economies, Moody's expected growth to slow to 2.6 per cent in 2026 from 2.8 per cent in 2025 and remain at 2.6 per cent in 2027 and 2028. Advanced economies were projected to grow by about 1.7 per cent in 2027 and 2028, while growth in emerging market economies was expected to ease from 4.5 per cent in 2025 to 3.8 per cent in 2026, before recovering to 4 per cent in 2027 and 2028. The agency said investment would remain a key source of global demand, led by spending on artificial intelligence (AI), digital infrastructure, defence and energy security. However, higher financing costs and weaker household purchasing power would offset some of the impetus. Moody’s also warned that a prolonged energy shock, renewed trade and geopolitical tensions, rising bond yields and disappointing returns from AI investments could weigh on global growth. It expected Brent crude prices to average $90 per barrel in 2027 and $80 in 2028, compared with an estimated $93 in 2026.

Bulls in action! Sensex zooms 1,400 pts intraday; oil, FII buying aid rally Experts said that strong FII participation in the past few sessions and better-than-expected corporate earnings are supporting the market rally.

Bulls in action! Sensex zooms 1,400 pts intraday; oil, FII buying aid rally

Abhinav Ranjan New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 11 2026 | 3:40 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Stock market today, Sensex today: Market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty 50 opened higher on Wednesday amid a correction in crude oil prices and heavy buying in financial stocks. Improving FII participation also supported the market sentiment.   The BSE Sensex made an intraday high of 82,520, up 1,411 points, or 1.74 per cent. Similarly, the 50-share Nifty benchmark touched a high of 25,424, up 380 points, or 1.52 per cent.   Experts said that strong FII participation in the past few sessions and better-than-expected corporate earnings are supporting the market rally. VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments, said that the sharp drop in crude oil prices is a relief for India.

"This surge was triggered mainly by aggressive FII buying. The dramatic change in the market environment was triggered by positive global cues for India from the weakening of the AI trade," he said.   The BSE Sensex closed 772.75 points, or 0.95 per cent higher at 81,879.40, while the Nifty 50 added 210.40 points, or 0.84 per cent, to settle at 25,255.05.   Also Read

Stock Market Close: Sensex pares gains but ends 773 pts up, Nifty at 25,255; PSU Bank rises 3%

Punjab National Bank share price soars 11% in two days; hits 52-week high

Bank Nifty tops 61,000, nears all-time high; what do charts say?

Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE     Stock market today, Sensex today rally: Key reasons    Oil prices fall: Oil prices fell to two-month lows in the previous session, as the market swung between hopes for a de-escalation in the US-Iran war. At the last check, Brent futures climbed 0.78 per cent to $92.20 a barrel. US WTI crude traded at $86.53.

"The drop in Brent crude to $92 is an additional macro relief for India," VK Vijayakumar said.   Easing geopolitical tensions: US President Donald Trump has downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran "at this point," easing fears of sustained supply disruptions from the West Asia. However, Trump, in a Reuters interview and a later appearance in the White House press briefing room, said he plans to keep up a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.   FPI inflows: VK Vijayakumar said that FPIs have turned aggressive buyers in the Indian stock market. In the past eight trading days, they pumped in over ₹55,000 crore into equities, the highest net inflows in the past six years.

"Given the new favourable environment for the Indian market, FIIs are likely to continue buying, imparting resilience to the frontline stocks in banking/financials, telecom, capital goods, select auto and pharmaceutical majors. This rally, which has more steam left, will be led again by large-caps," he said.   Banking & financial services shine: Today's rally was led by heavy buying in banking, and financial services stocks. At the close, the Nifty Bank index was up 1.76 per cent, with 13 of 14 constituents ending in the green. The Nifty Financial Services gained  1.02 per cent, with 17 out of 20 stocks finishing in the positive territory.

Strong earnings: VK Vijayakumar said that it is important to note that the real fundamental support to the rally has come from the better-than-expected Q2 results. The near 24 per cent earnings growth in Nifty 50 in Q2 is a 12 quarter high and has compressed the forward PE for Nifty 50 to fair levels.   Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

item.content:encoded:

All about Alice Huang, the Chinese banker linked to Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reports linking Huang to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who was accused of having ties to Beijing's intelligence service, have put Nvidia's chip exports and Megaspeed under scrutiny

Alice Huang (right) attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a restaurant in Taiwan in May 2025 | Photo: Reuters

AP Washington 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 11 2026 | 2:34 PM IST

Listen to This Article

She was building a career in Chinese finance before turning to tech with a leadership role at a data centre company in Singapore. He is the high-profile CEO of Nvidia, the California-based company that makes computer chips relied upon by advanced artificial intelligence systems. An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds. The Chinese businesswoman also known as Huang Le had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, according to reports over the past month by the New York Times. The newspaper also reported that top policymakers were informed in a memo that intelligence indicated she was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, recruited to influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available in China.

In one widely shared photograph of the pair, Jensen Huang and people surrounding him are holding drinks in Taipei, while Alice Huang sits behind him, apparently watching him in conversation. The picture was posted in 2024 by software company NetThunder to its LinkedIn page. Also Read

Why Nvidia dominates AI, and what Huang's scandal could cost the firm

Nvidia has no clear successor to Jensen Huang. Who could take over?

China, Asean advance South China Sea pact talks, push deal to next year

Microsoft presses Trump admin to scuttle ban on Chinese data center tech

Jensen Huang's close ties to Trump come under scrutiny after spy claim

It remains unclear how long the affair lasted, and when exactly the relationship might have ended. The Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment. Who is Alice Huang? Publicly available information about Alice Huang is scant. She was a Chinese finance executive before becoming involved in artificial intelligence, data centres and computer chips. In 2023, she became a director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which describes itself as an "NVIDIA cloud partner". Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the US over its alleged skirting of US export restrictions and routing of a large amount of advanced Nvidia chips for Chinese users.

Megaspeed was incorporated in 2015 in Singapore with the name 7Road International, after being spun off as the overseas arm of a Chinese video game developer, according to corporate registration records. Filings show that in March 2023, it renamed itself Megaspeed International, with all of the shares transferred to Huang Le Limited, a company registered in the British Virgin Islands. That same month, Alice Huang became Megaspeed's controlling shareholder, according to research by the C4ADS, a Washington-based nonprofit focused on global security. But by November 2023, she was no longer listed as a director at Megaspeed, and all her shares were transferred to a Singaporean businessman, Tan Yong Pong, who also is known as James Tan.

While public records suggest Alice Huang left Megaspeed, short seller Culper Research issued a report in May this year that cited a Megaspeed employee saying Huang was "actually still our boss" and was still involved in the company's daily operations. Before Megaspeed, Alice Huang previously held senior positions at the Chinese firm Shanghai Hexi Investment Co. from around 2015 to 2017, according to social media posts and records from Simuwang, a Chinese private equity database. Her roles at Hexi included deputy general manager, executive director and member of the investment committee, according to Hexi's social media posts, among possible other roles. Hexi's founder Kang Wei, who appeared on some records alongside Alice Huang, was fined in 2018 by China's securities regulator 400,000 yuan (USD 60,000) over financial misconduct behaviours while Hexi was fined 17.7 million yuan (USD 2.7 million).

Before that, Alice Huang worked at HSBC's Hong Kong private banking arm and at CITIC Securities, a Chinese investment bank. HSBC and CITIC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on her employment history. Beijing has refuted claims that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. Its Foreign Ministry said this week that the "Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China". Why Megaspeed is at the centre of the controversy With the emergence of the latest scandal, Singapore-based AI computing company Megaspeed, where Alice Huang was a senior executive, is once again under the spotlight. Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer, was originally incorporated in 2015 before changing its name to Megaspeed International in 2023. Nvidia lists Megaspeed as a partner on its website, while Megaspeed says on its website it's "a core business partner of NVIDIA's computing power cloud business in the Asia-Pacific region".

It was the overseas gaming arm of Shenzhen-based developer 7Road Holdings Ltd. Late last year, Megaspeed denied accusations following reports that it was routing Nvidia chips to China, saying in a statement on its website that "there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities". Singapore's government said in late October, after fresh reports that Alice Huang was accused of being a Chinese intelligence source, that authorities were investigating Megaspeed and that Singapore "does not condone businesses" circumventing or violating other countries' export controls. However, it said, there were no investigations conducted in respect to Alice Huang.

Megaspeed did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
